page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a shared-core virtual machine belonging to the e2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs allocated from a 1/8 shared physical core, supporting hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. It includes 1.0 GB of system memory, providing 0.5 GB of RAM per core, and does not include any local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results place the e2-micro in the bottom 10% across all tested performance categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 132.9 and 171.0, respectively. Memory performance is highly constrained, with a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 9.73 GB/sec, which drops to 0.1 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database and transactional operations are similarly limited, as demonstrated by a PassMark database score of 57.19 and a Redis SET throughput of 0.2 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is measured at 0.17 GB/sec.

Due to its shared-core resource allocation and low memory capacity, this instance offers a highly cost-efficient profile for minimal, non-resource-intensive tasks. It is designed for workloads that do not require sustained CPU performance or high memory bandwidth. Suitable applications include lightweight utility scripts, basic microservices, development environments, or low-traffic static web serving.

The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.
